title: Eventing store: retention, indexing & backfill runbook
content:
Purpose:
This note captures the design decisions and operational runbook for storing, indexing, exporting and backfilling event/audit data generated by RBAC v2 and other security surfaces. It focuses on retention tiering, indexing strategies, backfill mechanics, SIEM export expectations, and common failure modes with mitigation steps. Intended audience: security, infra, observability, SRE and platform owners responsible for the audit/event pipeline.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to structured audit events produced by services (auth, console, dedicated/private control plane, optimize) labeled with schema v2.
- Primary store is the eventing S3 bucket (encrypted) + OLAP index (BigQuery) + search index (OpenSearch).
- Kafka is the streaming backbone. Indexers subscribe from compliant topic prefixes (audit.*, evidence.*).
- SIEM export targets Splunk and our enterprise Elastic/SIEM via HEC and syslog connectors.
- RBAC v2 adds high-cardinality principal fields; retention/PII rules must be applied before long-term archival.

Event schema highlights (summary):
- event_id (uuid), event_ts (RFC3339), producer_service, env, principal_id (hashed for long-term storage), principal_cleartext (short TTL), action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, request_context (ip, user_agent), change_payload (diff), trace_id, schema_version
- Versioning: schema_version is required. Incompatibility results in messages routed to audit-schema-errors topic for manual triage.

Retention tiers and policy (practical):
- Hot (0-90 days): full event with principal_cleartext, change_payload, used for investigations and console queries. Indexed in OpenSearch with high replication factor and daily indices.
- Warm (90-365 days): principal_cleartext redacted, full event retained in S3 and BigQuery for analytics; OpenSearch indices rolled to warm nodes with reduced replicas.
- Cold (365-1825 days / 1-5 years): only minimal fields kept (event_id, event_ts, producer_service, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, trace_id). Sensitive payloads purged. BigQuery partitioned per month for cost efficiency.
- Archive (>5 years): policy-based export to long-term encrypted archive; kept only where legally required. Default retention 3 years unless contract/regulation requires longer.

Indexing strategy (OpenSearch):
- Index per week for hot indices (audit-hot-YYYY.WW). Mappings are explicit with typed fields to avoid dynamic mapping explosions.
- Use field aliasing for schema evolution (e.g., principal.user -> principal_id) and runtime fields for computed tokens.
- Partition keys: event_ts and producer_service. High-cardinality fields (principal_id, resource_id) are keyword fields but avoid frequent sorting on them.
- ILM policies: hot (7d), warm (83d), cold move triggers at 90d. Force-merge disabled for first 24h to avoid heavy I/O.

Primary ingestion pipeline (implementation notes):
1) Producer -> Kafka topic audit.<service> (producer validates schema v2 and attaches schema_version).
2) Stream processor (ksql/beam) enriches events (geoip, service metadata), computes dedup_key = sha256(event_id + producer_instance).
3) Transformer service writes canonical JSON to S3 (audit-events/yyyy=.../event_id.json) and forwards to indexer topic.
4) Indexer workers (k8s autoscaled) consume indexer topic, bulk-index into OpenSearch and write rows to BigQuery for OLAP. Indexer is idempotent via dedup_key and uses optimistic concurrency for updates.
5) SIEM connector consumes a filtered stream (only events flagged for SIEM export) and forwards to Splunk HEC and/or syslog-facing Elastic cluster.

Backfill design (safe and resumable):
- Backfills must be driven by the canonical S3 store as the source-of-truth. Indexer jobs must be able to start with a start_key and checkpoint progress to a backfill-checkpoints table in BigQuery.
- Backfill worker semantics: read S3 objects in lexicographic order, transform, compute dedup_key, bulk index with upsert by dedup_key, and commit checkpoint every 5k objects.
- Parallelization: partition by date prefix + producer_service to avoid hotspots. Each backfill shard gets an exclusive lock (Zookeeper or DynamoDB lease).
- Idempotency and dedup: indexer upserts on dedup_key; if schema has changed, apply a migration transform before indexing.
- Validation: after backfill completion, run a reconciliation job: sample N events and compare stored doc in OpenSearch/BigQuery vs S3. Discrepancies create tickets in JIRA backfill-<id>.

Failure modes and mitigations (operational playbook):
- Failure: High indexing error rate (mapping conflicts).
  Mitigation: divert to audit-schema-errors topic, pause indexing, run automated mapping upgrade tool in staging, apply explicit mappings, re-run small backfill. Use schema_version to route older versions to compatibility transformer.
- Failure: Repeated bulk timeouts and OOM on indexers.
  Mitigation: scale indexer pods vertically, lower batch sizes, enable backpressure on Kafka consumer, and throttle producer enrichment. Add circuit breaker that marks topic as degraded and forwards to cold storage-only path.
- Failure: SIEM export drops events due to HEC throttling.
  Mitigation: buffer to persistent queue (S3-backed), incrementally replay, and apply per-tenant rate limits. Alert: SIEM-export-error-rate > 1% for 15m triggers P1.
- Failure: Backfill collision (two workers reprocessing same prefix).
  Mitigation: implement lease/lock per shard and heartbeat. Detect stale leases older than 30m and provide a manual “reclaim” CLI for SRE.
- Failure: PII leakage in cold archive.
  Mitigation: run automated scrubbing job during tier transition. Keep audit of scrubbing actions (who ran, what keys removed). Any manual override requires SOC approval and is logged.

Monitoring, alerts and SLOs:
- Indexing latency SLO: 95% of audit events indexed within 60s of production.
- Delivery SLO to SIEM: 99% of flagged events delivered within 5m.
- Backfill progress metric: items_processed / items_expected with alert if velocity below threshold for 4 hours.
- Define dashboards: indexing_error_rate, es_bulk_failures, kafka_consumer_lag for audit topics, backfill_checkpoints_age, siem_export_queue_depth.
- Pager rules: sustained indexing_error_rate > 0.5% for 30m -> P1. Large backfill jobs failing 3x -> P2 escalation to infra and sec.

Evidence automation and deletion audit trail:
- Evidence artifacts (attachments, payload diffs) are referenced by object_id stored in canonical event. Actual binary is stored in a separate evidence-bucket with short TTL and separate KMS key.
- Deletion flow: 1) Deletion request recorded (ticket id), 2) automated scrubbing job removes sensitive fields and marks object deleted in an audit-deletions table with metadata (who, why, when), 3) event indices updated to reflect redaction and deletion marker, 4) retention timers enforce final archive removal. All steps record an immutable audit entry.
- RBAC v2 implications: deletion and redaction operations require two-person approval for high-privilege principals. RBAC audit events for approve/reject are kept in hot tier for 2 years.

SIEM export considerations:
- Only export a subset of fields to SIEM (deny payloads and PII unless explicitly authorized). Use field-mapping config that is versioned in Git.
- Splunk HEC: apply batching and HEC rate-limit handling, maintain per-workspace credentials and rotation.
- Syslog/CEF export: for backwards-compatibility, serialize a flattened subset and add event_type tags.
- Test plan: daily smoke tests that send synthetic events through full pipeline to verify delivery to SIEM and ingestion counts.

Cost & storage considerations:
- Hot OpenSearch indices are expensive; favour summarization for high-traffic producers and longer retention in BigQuery (cheaper per TB for analytics).
- Monthly cost review: correlate hot index size with query patterns; automate index lifecycle thresholds based on percentiles of query usage.

Operational checklists (runbook quick actions):
- If indexing fails: 1) pause indexer consumer group, 2) check mapping errors, 3) escalate to infra if ES cluster health degraded, 4) re-run transformer against schema-errors topic.
- If backfill stalls: inspect backfill-checkpoints table, check shard leases, verify S3 read permissions, restart single shard worker with --resume flag.
- If SIEM export shows gap: check SIEM connector logs, check buffer S3 prefix, run replay tool with --limit <n>.

Testing and pre-deployment validation:
- Canary flow: route 1% of live events to a canary index and SIEM workspace; validate mapping and delivery for 24h before promoting mapping changes.
- Chaos tests: simulate indexer pod OOM and Kafka broker unavailability; assert no data loss (events must land in S3) and graceful throttling.
- Backfill dry-run: run on a 24h window and validate end-to-end checksum reconciliation.

Open questions and TODOs:
- Decide default retention for clinical/regulatory customers (proposal: per-contract retention overrides implemented as metadata flags).
- Finalize redaction library and integrate into transformer service (owner: eng-security, ticket JIRA-SEC-475).
- Add automated legal hold mechanism that suspends deletion policies for specific org_ids (requires product + compliance signoff).

Appendix: useful commands and scripts
- Check indexer lag: kubectl logs deploy/indexer --since=1h | grep "consumer_lag"
- Reclaim shard lease: python scripts/reclaim_lease.py --shard audit-2024-11-05-prod-auth
- Launch resume backfill: python tools/backfill_runner.py --prefix audit-events/yyyy=2024/mm=11 --checkpoint_table backfill_checkpoints --resume

Notes/History:
- 2024-08: initial pipeline v1 deployed (no schema_version and single OpenSearch cluster).
- 2024-10: RBAC v2 rollout added high-cardinality principal fields; triggered need for redaction automation.
- 2024-11: canonical S3 store introduced as single source of truth for backfills and legal discovery.

If you find any missing operational detail in day-to-day runs, add a short note at the top of this doc with date and one-line summary so we can iterate this runbook.
